question: Compared to DKA, HHS typically presents with higher plasma glucose, greater dehydration, and absent or minimal ketonuria.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually true. HHS has more extreme hyperglycaemia and dehydration than DKA, but far less ketosis because the partial insulin activity in T2DM prevents uncontrolled lipolysis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. HHS features: glucose often >600 mg/dL (vs DKA usually 250-500), severe dehydration (8-10 L deficit vs ~5 L in DKA), serum osmolality >320 mOsm/kg, and minimal ketones because residual insulin blocks lipolysis.
